summary: Gorham, NH lookout set up in 1910, rebuilt 1915-16, cut back in 1922, destroyed in the 1938 hurricane; listed as gone; summit owned by a private camp.

facts.status_note: firelookout.org lists the tower as gone; NH Family Hikes reports four cement footings from the old fire tower on the official summit

access.note: Summit owned by the Horton Center, a private camp and worship center, per NH Family Hikes

visit.trail_note: About 3.5 miles out and back with a loop from the Pine Link Trail lot on Pinkham B Road; the road is seasonal and its gate status should be checked on TrailsNH

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1939 newspaper item and the NH Family Hikes list give 2,410 feet; the NH Family Hikes hike page gives 2404 feet. The story reports both and does not choose one.

sources.title: Fire Tower History - NH Family Hikes

notes_for_editor: Not cited because the source could not be read: Library of Congress 1943 photo records (loc.gov items 2017858046 and 2017878586, returned 403 to fetch_text) describe Barbara Mortensen as a fire and airplane lookout in a fire tower on Pine Mountain. If accurate, a tower stood there in 1943 despite the 1938 destruction line, which would fit the 1939 replacement plan but is unconfirmed. Also not cited: a Conway Daily Sun search snippet (article returned 429 on retries) says the upper part of a 165-foot NHPTV transmission tower on top of Pine Mountain in Gorham collapsed in high winds on January 16th; the year is not in the snippet. That would mean a broadcast tower stands on the summit today. Verify before writing the today section further. The NH state PDF forest-lookout-towers-history.pdf returned 403, and a Facebook 1965 photo caption (Gorham tower) is unverified. The brief record had no errors for this lookout.
